But this is a transplant-medicine record; per checker instructions such records are ANALOGIES and must never be phrased as 'supports'. relevance_to_tphe currently opens with 'supports R4 no-stake assessor' — FIX by rewording to 'analogous to R4 no-stake assessor (transplant-medicine analogy, not domain-matched)'.

Not a fabrication (it is a fair generic reading of 'dual relationship'), but should be marked as inference. relevance_to_tphe uses 'supports R4' for a psychotherapy-ethics analogy — FIX to analogy phrasing, and flag the subtype claim as interpretive.

Abstract quote: 'Ethical codes of practice of mental health professional bodies provide little guidance regarding non-sexual dual relationships' and 'Dual relationships are common in rural mental health practice.' Key finding accurate. relevance_to_tphe already uses 'complicates R4' (not 'supports') and explicitly frames this as a precautionary/non-outcome-trial-backed design choice — correctly hedged, no fix needed.

Matches key_finding; no numeric AUC value is claimed in either the abstract or the record, so nothing to overclaim. IPV domain, directly relevant.

A protocol for immediate referral and examination for further injury from strangulation should be adopted for IPV survivors at high risk.' AUC=.68 and the null strangulation-addition result and referral recommendation all match exactly.

Abstract quote: 'SARA risk assessments had significant predictive validity with respect to risk management recommendations made by police, as well as with recidivism... High levels of intervention were associated with decreased recidivism in high risk cases, but with increased recidivism in low risk cases.' Exact match, including the mediation direction.

n=190 matches; abstract confirms Indigenous individuals 'were assessed as demonstrating more risk factors and were more likely to be rated as high risk... more likely to recidivate.' relevance_to_tphe correctly uses 'complicates R4/P5', flags that independence alone doesn't remove other biases.
Abstract quote: 'CHW warm handoff rates increased two-fold over the intervention period.' Matches key_finding's 'doubled' framing exactly.

Abstract quote: 'Emergency staff screened 58.5% of eligible patients for social risk... Among interviewed patients, 57.1% recalled being screened, but only 24.5% recalled receiving resource guides... Of 13 observed discharge interactions, clinical staff only discussed guides with 2 patients... Staff expressed preference for warm handoff to social services.' The 58.5%, 24.5%, 2/13 and staff-preference figures are all correct, but the 24.5% figure is specifically among the interviewed THRIVE+ subsample, not literally 'of those screening positive' as a whole-cohort denominator. FIX wording to 'of interviewed screen-positive patients, only 24.5%...' for precision.

Abstract quote: 'IRR = 0.79... at 6 months (95% CI 0.61-1.01), 0.78... at 12 months (95% CI 0.64-0.95)... 0.78 at 24 months (95% CI 0.66-0.91)... no difference between the SMS and TAU groups in the time to first repeat self-harm event over 24 months (HR = 0.96, 95% CI 0.72-1.26)... But this is a self-harm/suicide-prevention RCT; per instructions such records are ANALOGIES to T-PHE's check-in and must not be phrased as 'supports (c)'. FIX relevance_to_tphe wording to explicit analogy framing (T-PHE claims no effectiveness, so citing an effect-size RCT as 'support' risks the check-in being read as validated).

Key finding accurate. Suicide-prevention domain record phrased as 'supports (c)' — FIX to analogy framing per instructions.

This is a teen-pregnancy-prevention-programme record (one of the three domains the instructions single out); relevance_to_tphe already uses 'complicates (d)' rather than 'supports', so the analogy framing itself is acceptable — only the title needs correction.

Actual PubMed title: 'Comparison of recidivism rates for a teenage trauma prevention program after the addition of high-fidelity patient simulation.' Record drops the word 'patient' — FIX title. Key finding numbers confirmed exactly: 'no significant difference was seen with or without simulation', 'recidivism rate was 55% within 6 years. At 6 months it was 8.4%, at 1 year it was 20%', 'decrease speed (30%)'. n=124 ('One hundred twenty-four students') matches. relevance_to_tphe correctly frames this as contradicting a naive fidelity=outcome assumption, not as direct support.

overall_note: All 24 PMIDs resolve and all key numeric findings (ODARA/SARA/DA/DA-5 AUCs and the 45% correct-administration figure, the SMS-SOS IRRs/HR and 22% reduction, the postpartum-navigation 80.7%/48.4% completion figures, the RCL/Lifestyle-Africa/teenage-trauma-simulation fidelity and completion percentages) check out verbatim against the PubMed abstracts — no fabricated statistics found. Two classes of problem recur: (1) five title strings have minor but real mismatches vs. the PubMed record (25383928, 41203119, 37191932, 31909412, 29185783) — all fixable by copying the exact PubMed ArticleTitle; (2) analogical-domain records (transplant medicine: 26287054, 26293351, 29708521; unrelated clinical-ethics fields: 26254909, 11649348; suicide/self-harm brief-contact trials: 38083861, 37321352, 36963515, 35855500) are worded with 'supports' in relevance_to_tphe even though the file's own gaps_noted section already concedes these are analogical, not domain-matched — per the checker's instruction these must never read as 'supports' and should be reworded as explicit analogies. One record (36963515, Radin 2023 CC vs CC+) has a more serious problem: its key_finding describes only what was tested and omits that the trial found NO significant difference in the primary outcome — this null result must be added. One record (33280504) has an unsupported interpretive clause appended to an otherwise-correct key_finding. No record was found to be out of scope, off-topic, or fabricated; 15 of 24 records are recommended KEEP-as-is or FIX-for-wording-only, with the null-result omission (36963515) being the one substantive evidentiary error found.
